title: One Tuesday, Twice
description: Run the worst day at a fictional 18-person service company, then build the system that ends it. An interactive case study with a playable simulation.
seoTitle: One Tuesday, Twice — An Interactive Case Study
seoDescription: A simulated Tuesday at a fictional 18-person service company, run twice: once with a scattered workflow, once with the system that replaced it. Every number is computed by a model you can inspect.
problem: Service businesses outgrow their informal workflow long before they outgrow their headcount. The cost is hard to see because it hides in coordination: re-keying, chasing, forgetting, apologizing.
solution: An interactive case study that lets the reader feel that cost instead of reading claims about it: play the worst day, build the six changes one at a time, then watch the same day run through the system. A deterministic simulation model computes every number.
result: The same day, both ways: 30 of 56 requests handled with 9.3 hours of coordination, or 53 of 56 with about zero. The piece ends by turning the mirror on the reader's own operation.
